chunks: Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about selling the juice of the grapes to the one who makes it into a Prohibited (substance). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. You can sell it as a Permissible (substance), so he makes that into a Prohibited (substance). May Allah distance him and break him.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell grape juice to someone who will turn it into wine?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'salamah al-'aqd' (validity of the contract) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the intrinsic permissibility of the commodity (grape juice) and the extrinsic usage by the buyer. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) asserts that the seller's transaction remains halal even if the buyer converts it to haram, emphasizing that the prohibition attaches to the consumer's action rather than the sale itself. This ruling underscores the Shia view that the seller is not liable for the buyer's subsequent misuse, provided the commodity itself is pure and permissible.
